evidence_summary: Source units v7u_N002879 and v7u_N002882 explain RBC's lack of documented governance and failure to develop policies, directly illustrating the governance oversight component listed in target unit v7u_N002873. Source unit v7u_N002881 explicitly states the case illustrates weak oversight, linking to the overall AFC program concept in v7u_N002871.

Source units v7u_N002904 and v7u_N002905 state the requirement for a policy adoption protocol and features of good policies, which ground the target units' prescriptions for policy development, approval, accessibility, and communication.

Source units v7u_N002910 and v7u_N002911 explain jurisdictional compliance and exception management, which ground the target units' rules on tailoring policies, conducting gap analyses, and aligning local policies with global standards.

Source units define governance committees and their structural requirements (v7u_N002930, v7u_N002931, v7u_N002932, v7u_N002933), which ground the purpose and benefits of internal reporting to those committees (v7u_N002949, v7u_N002950).

Source units v7u_N002936–v7u_N002939 classify key governance committees (Board risk, AML governance, High-risk customer review, Sanctions oversight), which ground the target units v7u_N002954–v7u_N002958 that describe typical internal AFC report contents (KRIs, KPIs, regulatory updates, audit findings, high-risk customer reports) tailored to those committees.

Source units define regulatory reporting as a critical obligation (v7u_N002960), note jurisdictional variation (v7u_N002961), and state consequences of non-compliance (v7u_N002962). These ground the target units which specify UK-specific reports (v7u_N002978, v7u_N002979) and requirements for accuracy, timeliness, and confidentiality (v7u_N002981, v7u_N002982, v7u_N002983).
Source units define regulatory reporting as a critical obligation and explain jurisdictional variation, grounding the target units which state specific US FinCEN reporting rules.

Source units introduce the control framework and list KYC/CDD as the first customer lifecycle control, establishing the foundation for later-stage controls. Target units describe investigation escalation and SAR filing, which are later-stage controls that depend on the initial KYC/CDD framework.

Source units introduce the customer lifecycle control framework (v7u_N002997, v7u_N002998) and classify KYC/CDD at onboarding as the first control (v7u_N002999), grounding the periodic review and ongoing due diligence methods described in target units (v7u_N003004–v7u_N003007).

Source units v7u_N002997 and v7u_N002998 introduce the customer lifecycle framework and its controls, grounding the offboarding and exit strategy rules in target units v7u_N003008 and v7u_N003009 as the final stage of that lifecycle.

Source units state the risk-based KYC requirement (v7u_N003011) and define KYC (v7u_N003012), which ground the target units explaining customer risk assessment (v7u_N003027), risk scoring (v7u_N003028), and due diligence processes (v7u_N003029).

Source units state the risk-based due diligence requirement (v7u_N003011) and define KYC as a core AFC compliance process (v7u_N003012), which directly ground the target unit's definition of EDD as a deeper verification process for high-risk customers (v7u_N003030).

Source units state the risk-based due diligence requirement (v7u_N003011) and define KYC as assessing customer risks (v7u_N003012), which directly ground the target unit's measure of rejecting customers when risk is unacceptable (v7u_N003031).

Source units state the risk-based KYC requirement (v7u_N003011) and define KYC as a core AFC compliance process (v7u_N003012), which directly ground the target units describing risk-based KYC refresh cycles (v7u_N003032) and the triggering of enhanced due diligence for higher risk (v7u_N003033).

Source units define the risk-based KYC framework (v7u_N003011, v7u_N003012), which directly grounds the ongoing screening obligations for sanctions, PEPs, and adverse news stated in target units (v7u_N003034, v7u_N003035).

Source units state the risk-based KYC requirement (v7u_N003011) and define KYC as a core AFC process (v7u_N003012), which grounds the target unit's description of transaction monitoring as a dynamic risk-adjustment process (v7u_N003037).

Source units v7u_N003011 and v7u_N003012 establish the risk-based KYC requirement, which grounds the CRA definition in v7u_N003040 and its key risk elements in v7u_N003042–v7u_N003046. The risk-based principle directly underpins the evaluation of customer risk factors.

Source units state the risk-based KYC requirement and define KYC as a core AFC compliance process, which directly grounds the target units that define KYC for natural persons and classify its components.

Source units state the risk-based KYC requirement (v7u_N003011) and define KYC as a core AFC compliance process (v7u_N003012), which directly ground the target units that define KYC for legal persons (v7u_N003076) and list its components (v7u_N003077).

Source unit v7u_N003039 summarizes the comprehensive risk-based KYC framework by stating its benefits: enhanced AFC compliance, mitigated financial crime risks, and alignment with international obligations. Target units v7u_N003011 and v7u_N003012 introduce the regulatory requirement and definition of risk-based KYC, which are directly summarized by the source.
